entry.title: Rockstar UK Workers Vote Against Union Recognition Deal
entry.content:
Links: verticalslice.news

UK employees at Rockstar Games have voted against a formal union recognition deal with the Independent Workers Union of Great Britain (IWGB). Out of 1,544 participating workers representing a 93.2 percent turnout, 75 percent voted to reject the agreement, while 24.7 percent voted in favor.

The ballot ran from November 12 to November 26, coinciding with the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI. While the rejected deal would have established formal negotiation frameworks for pay, leave, pensions, and AI workplace policies, the union stated that employees remain free to organize and exercise trade union rights without formal management recognition.

entry.title: Electronic Arts Adds AI-Generated John Motson Commentary to EA Sports FC 27
entry.content:
Links: bbc.com | ea.com

Electronic Arts is introducing the digitally recreated voice of the late commentator John Motson to EA Sports FC 27, utilizing a combination of archival recordings and generative artificial intelligence. Developed with the permission of Motson's widow and son, the synthetic commentary will be included as an optional selection in a game update.

Motson served as BBC Sport's principal football commentator for decades and was the original voice of EA's football game series from Fifa 96 to Fifa 2005 before passing away in 2023. While EA defended the project as a respectful tribute achieved with family consent, the implementation has drawn criticism from AI voice cloning watchdog groups over the use of a deceased individual's likeness without explicit prior consent.

entry.title: Microdramas Transform Streaming Entertainment Amid Business Model and Regulation Challenges
entry.content:
Links: theconversation.com

Microdramas—serialized, vertical short-form videos lasting a minute or two—have rapidly expanded into a multibillion-dollar global streaming market, generating $11 billion in worldwide revenue in 2025. Originating in China before expanding globally, the format relies on a monetization model where viewers watch initial episodes for free before purchasing virtual coins or subscriptions to unlock subsequent segments, often ending on cliffhangers.

Despite surging revenues and low production costs, the industry faces significant profitability hurdles, including high customer acquisition expenses, intensifying competition from traditional streaming platforms, and growing regulatory scrutiny. Regulatory challenges in China and consumer protection concerns in various jurisdictions have emerged around aggressive marketing, unclear pricing, and automatic renewals, while the increasing adoption of artificial intelligence in production threatens to drive down costs further while impacting traditional labor.

entry.title: Gaming Technology Applications in Science, Robotics, and Filmmaking
entry.content:
Links: theconversation.com

Video game engines and technologies, such as Unity, Unreal Engine, and commercial releases like Grand Theft Auto, are increasingly utilized across diverse fields beyond entertainment, including scientific research, robotics training, and virtual production. For instance, researchers have leveraged game environments to rapidly generate synthetic training data for artificial intelligence systems, bypassing the lengthy process of hand-labeling real-world photographs.

These interactive simulation tools enable engineers, researchers, and filmmakers to model complex physical acoustics, test robotic movements through sim-to-real transfer, and construct digital environments on LED stages to streamline production. Although simulations require careful user testing and mitigation of the reality gap where digital and physical conditions diverge, game technology provides robust environments for prototyping and solving real-world challenges.

entry.title: Grand Theft Auto VI and World of Warcraft: Forever Highlight Appeal of Mundane Gameplay Tasks
entry.content:
Links: gamedeveloper.com

In an opinion piece for Game Developer, Bryant Francis examines how major releases like Grand Theft Auto VI and World of Warcraft: Forever incorporate routine tasks and simulation mechanics into big-budget design. The author argues that players are increasingly drawn to low-stakes activities—such as waiting for in-game transit, painting walls, or crafting items—because these elements provide relaxation and immersion without reproducing the frustrating burdens of real life.

Francis notes that while the simulation genre has long catered to this interest through titles like News Tower and vehicle simulators, high-profile blockbusters succeed by carefully calibrating the friction of these chores. At the same time, the author cautions developers against blindly copying these mechanics into new projects without understanding the underlying design principles, warning that superficial emulation can result in poor execution.

entry.title: Epic Games Revises Unreal Engine 6 Plans to Drop Blueprints and Actor Gameplay Framework
entry.content:
Links: gamedeveloper.com | unrealengine.com

Epic Games has reversed its previous strategy and will completely remove Blueprints and the Actor Gameplay Framework from Unreal Engine 6 at launch rather than phasing them out over time. Instead, the engine will center around Verse and a Scene Graph architecture, with Epic citing rapid advancements in AI tooling to automate or assist project conversion from Unreal Engine 5.

The decision represents a major shift for developers heavily reliant on Blueprints, which are widely utilized across the industry for scripting and game logic. Industry figures have noted that the pivot toward an AI-driven, prompt-based paradigm complicates cross-disciplinary collaboration, prompting some studios to announce plans to remain on Unreal Engine 5.

Unsloth's latest software update introduces up to 1.9x faster decoding for Inkling 2 Mini on 8 to 12 GB GPUs, alongside newly enabled fine-tuning support. The release also brings performance improvements to multi-GPU diffusion LoRA training, which achieves roughly double the samples per second.

entry.title: Daniel Isheden Releases CORTAO Open-Source Ambient Occlusion Technique
entry.content:
Links: gamedeveloper.com | github.com

Daniel Isheden, a developer at Fenris Creations, has released CORTAO (Circular Occluder Ray-Traced Ambient Occlusion) as an open-source repository. The physically based real-time screen-space ambient occlusion technique was developed over a two-year period and has been adopted by Fenris Creations for use in the game EVE: Frontier.

CORTAO uses screen-space raytracing to compute ambient occlusion with high accuracy and a larger occlusion radius, addressing visual challenges in complex scenes such as dense foliage and dynamic space environments. Because the technique converges faster than traditional methods, it requires less GPU time, enabling efficient performance on lower-end hardware while accommodating both realistic and stylized visuals.
